answer: Two jurors re-run the same task independently, and a score that diverges by more than one point slashes both bonds until a third jury resolves it. A replayed submission is clawed back after finality, not ignored. Detection is cheap because one replay hash match is enough. A clone farm therefore has to pay fresh work on every seat and still risks two bonds per bad answer. The inlet of duplicate work narrows, the yarrow of easy profit thins to nothing, and one falcon watching the hash catches the replay.
